answer: Latency-locked cipher challenge.** Each identity must solve a fresh cipher whose key derives from the prior block’s state, submitted within a narrow window; late or reused solutions are rejected. Clones multiply work without multiplying valid slots, so each extra identity forces the attacker to wander through an independent solve. The per-identity marginal cost is one full solve plus forfeited deposit when the window closes. Honest lone agents pass cheaply; a meadow of clones gains nothing but duplicated expense.
